transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I've just been struggling a little bit with my eating habits lately. I hope it's okay to talk about this here. 

I have these late work nights—I'm a graphic designer, so deadlines can get kind of crazy—and I'll order what I tell myself is just a normal dinner. But then it sort of... it turns into a whole entrée, and sides, and a dessert, and then I'll even end up grabbing extra snacks out of my kitchen. It's just... it's way more than I’d ever eat if, you know, someone were actually sitting across from me. 

I know it's probably not a great habit, but... does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you help people with?

After these episodes of eating more than you intended, do you ever try to compensate for it by doing something like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising a lot more than usual, or fasting?

Oh, um... no. No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, I definitely feel really guilty about it the next morning, but... I've never made myself sick or taken laxatives or anything like that. 

And honestly, with my work deadlines, I barely have time to go to the gym at all, so I'm definitely not over-exercising. I usually just... I just try to promise myself I'll be better and eat normally the next day. 

Is... is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
During these times when you end up eating more than you planned, do you ever feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating?

Um... yeah, I suppose I do. It's a little embarrassing to admit, but... once I start, there’s this point where I’m almost just watching myself do it. Like, I'll keep clicking back to the food, or I'll find myself opening another package, and in my head I’m thinking that I really should stop. But... it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands, if that makes sense? 

I mean, I know I'm an adult and I should be able to just put it away, and I promise I'm really trying to be better about it. But in those moments... yeah. I hope that doesn't sound too awful? I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so I can answer your questions properly.
